title: Collecting and Summarising Data: Samples, Averages and Spread
seo_title: Grade 8 Collecting and Summarising Data Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_code: Grade 8: 5.1 Collect, organise and summarise data
standard_text: Distinguish between samples and populations and suggest appropriate samples for investigation; organise numerical data in different ways in order to summarise by determining measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) and measures of dispersion (range, extremes, outliers).
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 8 data handling worksheets: samples, mean, median, mode, range, frequency tables and grouped data. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Mean from a table: Σ(value × frequency) ÷ total.
key_sub: Order the data for the median.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A sample is part of a population. A good sample is random and large enough.
  • Mean = total ÷ number of values. Median = middle value in order. Mode = most common.
  • Range = highest − lowest.
  • From a frequency table: mean = sum of (value × frequency) ÷ total frequency.

Examples

Example

Scores 1, 2, 3 with frequencies 4, 5, 1

(4 + 10 + 3) ÷ 10

Answer: mean 1,7

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Median without orderingOrder the data first.
Dividing by the wrong numberDivide by the total frequency.
A biased sampleChoose people at random.

items.q: A random sample of 200 adults in a town of 5 000 finds that 25 want a new swimming pool. Estimate how many adults in the town want the pool.
In a random sample, 35% of the trees in a forest have a disease. The forest has 1 200 trees. Estimate how many have the disease.
In a random sample, 8% of the trees in a forest have a disease. The forest has 2 500 trees. Estimate how many have the disease.
Rangers catch 60 fish in a lake, tag them and release them. Later they catch 100 fish and 4 are tagged. Estimate the number of fish in the lake.
items.e: 4 out of 100 caught are tagged, so the 60 tagged fish are about 4/100 of the lake. 60 × 100 ÷ 4 = 1 500.

items.q: In a random sample, 8% of the trees in a forest have a disease. The forest has 1 200 trees. Estimate how many have the disease.

In a random sample of 40 learners from a school of 600, 31 catch the bus. Estimate how many learners in the whole school catch the bus.
items.e: 31 out of 40 is 0,775 of the sample. 0,775 × 600 = 465.

items.q: A sample shows the text messages sent in a day by 5 learners: 15, 8, 10, 2, 10. What is the range?
items.e: Range = largest − smallest = 15 − 2 = 13.
